clips.text: Listen carefully. Our friend is looking for a partner. Can you find the animal that looks and sounds the same?
Two together! Draw a trail from your animal friends to the glowing ramp. Let's help them into the ark!
Look closely at our friend, then listen to its call. Find the animal with the same shape and sound.
Start at either animal and draw all the way to the glowing ramp. You can try any trail you like!
Sixteen animals! Eight pairs, all safely aboard. Noah listened to God, and you helped him care for every animal. Great work!
Lions greet one another by rubbing their heads. A lion's roar helps other lions find it.
Wolves live in family groups called packs. They howl to stay in touch. Can you make a gentle howl?
A tiger's stripes help it hide in tall grass. Look closely at the beautiful pattern on its coat.
Monkeys use calls to talk to their group. This recording is a macaque monkey. Can you answer its call?
An elephant uses its trunk to smell, drink, and pick things up. Can you curl your arm like a trunk?
Sheep recognize familiar voices. A little lamb can find its mother by listening to her bleat.
Cows use moos to call to one another. A calf learns to recognize its mother's voice.
Horses move their ears toward sounds. Their hooves make a clip-clop rhythm as they walk.
Two animals. One pair!
Four animals. Two pairs!
Six animals. Three pairs!
Eight animals. Four pairs!
Ten animals. Five pairs!
Twelve animals. Six pairs!
Fourteen animals. Seven pairs!
Sixteen animals. Eight pairs!
